messages:
Elliot Price: trying to lock docs plan for the SDK parity release. main questions:
1) where do we put retry/timeout/streaming “standard behavior” guidance (SDK pages vs API docs vs separate “Client behavior” page)
2) migration guide structure
3) snippets: keep identical semantics across python/ts/go (even if code differs)

Wei Chen: +1. also we should decide whether quickstarts get updated inline vs a “Troubleshooting + Reliability” section.

Ibrahim Khan: for (1), I’d like one canonical doc entry point that’s not language-specific, then each SDK page links to it + has code examples. we have the confluence spec pages but we need public docs.

Dana Lo: agree. in TS docs today we have a short “Retries” section but it’s different from python. if we do a shared page, it needs to call out the defaults (max attempts, backoff) + how to override per-request.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go users care about context cancellation semantics. I’d rather not bury that only in Go docs; it should be on the shared page under “Timeouts + cancellation” with language callouts.

Elliot Price: proposal:
- Add a new top-level docs page under “SDKs” called “Client behavior (auth, retries, timeouts, streaming)”
- That page describes the standard behavior + tables for defaults
- Each SDK page gets a consistent section: Auth / Retries / Timeouts / Streaming / Observability hooks
- Each section has copy-pasteable snippets for python/ts/go

Wei Chen: where exactly in nav? current nav is “SDKs -> Python, TypeScript, Go”. we can add “SDKs -> Reliability & client behavior” (or similar) above the language pages.

Henry Cho: naming: “Client behavior” is ok but might read internal. what about “SDK networking behavior” or “Retries & timeouts”? customers search those terms.

Monica Patel: +1 to customer-centric naming. also please make sure migration guidance is prominent; support is going to get tickets if retry defaults change.

Elliot Price: ok, maybe:
- “SDK networking: auth, retries, timeouts, streaming”
then each SDK page links to it.

Ibrahim Khan: works. on migration guide: I think we need 1 cross-SDK migration doc AND per-SDK changelog entries. migration doc should be scenario-based:
- “If you rely on no retries today”
- “If you set global timeouts”
- “If you stream responses”

Sabrina James: from examples side, I can update quickstarts + reference apps, but need a stable set of “recommended” snippets. can we standardize on the same env var name + config key names in docs? otherwise it’ll look inconsistent.

Dana Lo: env var is already the main inconsistency. TS examples show `REDWOOD_API_KEY` but python quickstart has `REDWOOD_TOKEN` in one place (old). we should pick one and fix all snippets.

Mateusz Zielinski: +1. Go docs currently mention `REDWOOD_API_KEY` and header `Authorization: Bearer ...`.

Ibrahim Khan: spec direction is `REDWOOD_API_KEY` as primary. header should be `Authorization: Bearer <key>` consistently. (Security wanted no alternate headers unless enterprise requirement.)

Elliot Price: great. action items for docs:
- audit and replace any `REDWOOD_TOKEN` occurrences
- ensure header is “Authorization: Bearer …” everywhere
- add note: keys must not be logged; examples should not print env vars

Wei Chen: migration guide structure suggestion (single page):
1. Summary of changes (what changed / why)
2. Breaking vs non-breaking (per SDK version)
3. Auth changes (env var, header normalization)
4. Retry changes (defaults, retryable statuses, retry-after)
5. Timeout changes (connect/read/overall; streaming read behavior)
6. Streaming changes (disconnect handling; cancellation)
7. How to keep old behavior (config flags / set retries=0 / etc)
8. Troubleshooting (common errors + request-id)

Connor O'Brien: please include “Release rollout plan” as internal-only section? or keep that out of public docs.

Elliot Price: public docs shouldn’t include rollout plan. we can add a short note like “If you see unexpected behavior, pin to previous version and contact support.”

Henry Cho: we should align language for changelog + migration doc. Product wants to say “Improved reliability defaults” not “Changed retry behavior” 😅. but migration doc must be explicit.

Wei Chen: re snippets: I suggest we keep the same logical structure across languages:
- client init with api key (from env)
- set a request timeout
- show retry customization
- streaming example with cancellation
Even if the code differs, headings + comments should be the same.

Dana Lo: streaming cancellation in TS should show `AbortController`. and note: “aborting does not retry, it surfaces cancellation.”

Mateusz Zielinski: Go snippet should show `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(...)` for non-streaming and `context.WithCancel` for streaming, and clarify how timeout vs cancel error surfaces.

Ibrahim Khan: also we should document the “safe retry” stance for streaming: no automatic resume on mid-stream disconnect; surface error with request-id; caller can decide to re-issue idempotent request.

Elliot Price: yep. let’s put that prominently to avoid people thinking we “guarantee” streaming resume.

Sabrina James: for quickstarts, I can add a small “Reliability defaults” section at the end:
- recommended timeouts
- retries: leave defaults, override only if you understand 429 behavior
- streaming: handle disconnects + show cancel

Wei Chen: where do we define the default numbers? I don’t want to hardcode values if they might change.

Ibrahim Khan: defaults are part of the standard and should be stable for this release. we can put a small table. if they change later, we update one page.

Elliot Price: ok, I’ll create the new shared page and make SDK pages link to anchor sections.
TODOs:
- [Elliot] draft “SDK networking: auth, retries, timeouts, streaming” page + table of defaults
- [Wei] outline migration guide w/ the 8 sections above + placeholders for per-SDK version notes
- [Dana/Mateusz] provide canonical snippets (auth + retry override + timeout + streaming cancel)
- [Sabrina] sync quickstarts/examples with the canonical snippets once ready

Henry Cho: please add a “What’s changing?” callout box at top of migration guide with 3 bullets, and a “No action needed if…” section.

Monica Patel: +1 and make sure it links to request-id guidance (Support needs that).

Elliot Price: will do. also adding a note: “Include request-id when contacting support” and “SDK surfaces request-id on errors” (if true across SDKs).

Dana Lo: TS currently doesn’t always expose request-id on streaming errors. I’m fixing in PR but docs should say “when available” until merged.

Mateusz Zielinski: Go does expose it for non-streaming; streaming is tricky but we can include it in the error wrapper. I’ll confirm.

Elliot Price: for now migration doc can say: “Errors include `request-id` when returned by the API; for streaming disconnects, capture the last seen request-id header at stream start.”

Wei Chen: sounds good. I’ll start the migration guide in docs repo today.

Elliot Price: thanks all. I’ll drop draft links here once up.

Henry Cho added a reaction: :thumbsup:

Monica Patel added a reaction: :white_check_mark:
